name: input
title: Input
description: UI SDK Input, InputGroup and InputClear (clears and returns focus).
docs: `<Field><FieldLabel>Name</FieldLabel><Input /></Field>`; `InputGroup` wraps it with icons and an `InputClear`. **Secrets:** `<Input sensitive />` is for an API key, a token or any value that mustn't leak. A controlled input (`value` with `onValueChange`, as every `FormField` binds it) makes React write the value into the DOM `value` attribute, where anything that reads attributes, the agent tree included, finds it. A sensitive input is uncontrolled and takes no `value` or `defaultValue` (it throws if given one): it is UI SDK's password field, which agents read as `[redacted]` even while shown, though they can still `setValue` it, under `data-agent-secret`. `autoComplete` is `new-password` by default rather than `off`, which browsers ignore on password fields: it keeps a saved sign-in password from being filled into it. `spellCheck`, `autoCapitalize` and `autoCorrect` are off, and `data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore` and `data-bwignore` ask password managers not to offer to save it. `revealable` adds a Show toggle (`revealLabel`, overridable) that switches the type between password and text and hides it again when its form submits and when the page is hidden. Read it with a `ref` or `sensitiveController={createPasswordInputController()}` (`getValue()`, `clear()`), or put it in a `FormField`, which reads it on submit and clears it (see Form). A sensitive input passes `id`, `className`, `style`, every `data-*` and `aria-*` attribute, `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `placeholder`, `tabIndex`, `maxLength`, `minLength`, `pattern`, `inputMode`, `autoComplete` and the focus, blur, click, pointer and mouse handlers; anything else is dropped, so nothing can write the value into an attribute.
